component-names.reason: Both Command namespaces expose Input, List, Item, Group, Separator, Empty, Loading and Dialog, and a palette built from them renders every part.

basic-tree-structure.reason: Both render the canonical tree alike: items in source order, the input placeholder, the separator, and no Empty text while items match.

parts-present.reason: Both render the root, input, list, item, group, group heading, group items, separator and loading parts on first render, each under its own attribute (`cmdk-*` in cmdk, `data-command-*` in modern-cmdk), and neither shows Empty while items exist.

state-attributes.reason: cmdk marks the active item with data-selected="true" and writes data-selected and data-disabled as "true" or "false" on every item. modern-cmdk marks the active item with a bare data-active and a disabled item with a bare data-disabled. Rewrite CSS that targets [data-selected="true"] to [data-active], and [data-disabled="true"] to [data-disabled].

large-list-rendered-count.reason: cmdk renders all 150 items. modern-cmdk virtualizes a list of more than 100 matches and renders only a window of them (12 here), so a test or script that counts rendered items sees fewer; pass virtualize={false} to Command.List to render every item.

large-list-height-property.reason: Both lists hold the measured height (137.5px) on their custom property for a 150-item list. modern-cmdk keeps its last non-virtual measurement while the list is virtual, so the property does not follow the virtual content height.

list-height-property.reason: Both lists write their measured height rounded to one decimal and suffixed with px to a custom property: `--cmdk-list-height` in cmdk and `--command-list-height` in modern-cmdk. Rename the property in CSS that reads it.

input-aria.reason: Both inputs are comboboxes with aria-expanded="true", aria-autocomplete="list" and aria-controls pointing at the list.

activedescendant-timing.reason: cmdk sets aria-activedescendant on the input only after the first arrow-key move. modern-cmdk sets it from the first render, to the item that is active then.

root-label.reason: cmdk renders the root label as a visually hidden <label cmdk-label> that the input names itself with through aria-labelledby. modern-cmdk renders no label element: the root is role="search" with aria-label, and the input carries the same aria-label.

list-role.reason: Both lists are role="listbox" and both items are role="option".

list-default-label.reason: Without a label, cmdk names the list "Suggestions" and modern-cmdk names it after the root label, which defaults to "Command palette". Pass a list label to name it explicitly.

list-label-prop.reason: A list label sets the list aria-label in both. cmdk takes it as the label prop of Command.List; modern-cmdk takes the aria-label prop of Command.List.

aria-selected-follows-active.reason: Both set aria-selected="true" on the active item and "false" on the others, and the value follows the arrow keys.

empty-visibility.reason: Both show Empty only while no item matches the search and hide it again when a match returns.

empty-aria.reason: cmdk renders Empty with role="presentation". modern-cmdk renders it with role="status" and aria-live="polite", so a screen reader announces it.

loading-aria.reason: cmdk renders Loading as role="progressbar" with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-label="Loading...". modern-cmdk renders it as role="status" with aria-busy="true" and aria-live="assertive", and shows it only while its loading prop or the palette is loading.

group-aria.reason: cmdk marks the group element role="presentation" and puts role="group" and aria-labelledby on the group-items element. modern-cmdk puts role="group" and aria-labelledby on the group element and gives the group-items element no role. Both hide the heading with aria-hidden.

group-hidden-no-match.reason: A group with no matching item hides itself with the hidden attribute in cmdk and with an inline display: none in modern-cmdk. In both, the unmatched items leave the DOM. CSS that targets [hidden] on a group does not apply to modern-cmdk.

separator-aria.reason: cmdk renders a separator with role="separator". modern-cmdk renders it with role="none", because it is only presentational inside a listbox.

separator-default-search.reason: By default cmdk hides a separator while a search is active, and modern-cmdk 1.x keeps it because alwaysRender defaults to true there. Pass alwaysRender={false} for cmdk's behaviour; the default becomes false in 2.0.

separator-always-render-true.reason: With alwaysRender set to true both libraries keep the separator while a search is active.

separator-always-render-false.reason: With alwaysRender set to false both libraries hide the separator while a search is active.

filter-by-query.reason: Both keep only the items that match the typed query and make the only match active.

filter-cleared.reason: After the search is cleared both show every item in source order. cmdk makes the first item active again; modern-cmdk keeps the item that was active for the search (banana here).

filter-ranking-order.reason: Both rank apple first for "apple". cmdk re-orders the DOM by rank and makes the top match active. modern-cmdk keeps the item that was active before the search while it still matches, so here applesauce stays active and Enter selects it, and in 1.7 it leaves the DOM in source order, which RA-02 changes to rank order in 1.8.0.

first-match-active.reason: Both make the first match active when the item that was active before the search no longer matches.

keywords.reason: Both match an item by its keywords as well as by its value.

custom-filter-ranking.reason: Both keep the items a custom filter scores above 0 and make the best-scored item active first, then step by score with the arrow keys. cmdk re-orders its DOM by score; modern-cmdk 1.7 leaves the DOM in source order, which RA-02 changes in 1.8.0. cmdk's filter prop is (value, search, keywords) and modern-cmdk's is (item, query).

custom-filter-exclusion.reason: In both, a custom filter that returns 0 excludes the item. modern-cmdk also excludes an item for false or a negative score.

custom-filter-arguments.reason: A custom filter sees the item value, the search and the item keywords in both. cmdk passes them as three arguments; modern-cmdk passes the item and the query, and the item holds the value and keywords.

filtering-off.reason: With filtering off both keep every item shown whatever is typed and never show Empty. cmdk takes shouldFilter={false}; modern-cmdk takes filter={false}.

force-mount.reason: cmdk's forceMount keeps an item shown through any search. modern-cmdk has no forceMount, so the item is filtered out like any other; give it a keyword or a filter that always matches.

arrow-navigation.reason: Both move the active item down and up with ArrowDown and ArrowUp.

home-end.reason: Both jump to the first item with Home and to the last with End.

loop-default.reason: Without a loop prop cmdk stops at the first and last item, and modern-cmdk wraps around, because loop defaults to true there. Pass loop={false} for cmdk's behaviour.

loop-true.reason: With loop set to true both wrap from the last item to the first and from the first to the last.

loop-false.reason: With loop set to false both stop at the first and last item.

vim-bindings.reason: cmdk moves the active item with Ctrl+N and Ctrl+J (down) and Ctrl+P and Ctrl+K (up) by default; vimBindings={false} turns that off (see vim-bindings-off). modern-cmdk has no vim bindings: those keys do nothing. Bind them yourself with a key handler on the root if you rely on them.

vim-bindings-off.reason: With vimBindings={false} cmdk stops Ctrl+N, J, P and K moving the active item. modern-cmdk has no vim bindings and no vimBindings prop, so those keys never move it; drop the prop.

modifier-arrows.reason: In cmdk Alt+ArrowDown and Alt+ArrowUp jump to the first item of the next or previous group, and Meta+ArrowDown and Meta+ArrowUp jump to the last and first item. modern-cmdk ignores those modifiers and moves one item like a plain arrow key.

selection-targets.reason: cmdk makes the clicked item active. modern-cmdk makes an item active on pointer move or the keyboard, not on click, so a tap or a programmatic click leaves the active item where it was (with a mouse, the pointer move before the click makes it active in both).

select-callback-arguments.reason: cmdk passes the item's value to onSelect, on a click and on Enter. modern-cmdk 1.x calls onSelect with no argument, and the value argument arrives in 2.0: until then read the value from your own item data.

disabled-items.reason: In both, a disabled item does not select on a click or Enter and the arrow keys step over it.

pointer-move-activates.reason: Both make an item active when the pointer moves over it.

default-value.reason: cmdk's defaultValue on the root sets the item that is active at mount. modern-cmdk has no defaultValue, so the first item is active at mount. To start on another item, control the active item with activeId and onActiveChange.

disable-pointer-selection.reason: cmdk's disablePointerSelection stops a pointer move from making an item active. modern-cmdk has no such prop: a pointer move over an item always makes it active.

item-id-prop.reason: cmdk spreads your props and then writes its own generated id, so an id on Command.Item does not reach the DOM. modern-cmdk uses the id prop as the item's DOM id and its registration id.

group-id-prop.reason: In both, the id prop on Command.Group is the group element's DOM id.

input-change-callback.reason: Typing calls the input's onValueChange with the new text in both, and the input shows it.

input-controlled-value.reason: In both, a controlled input value drives the search and holds when the parent does not apply a typed change, and the callback still hears the typing. The prop names match: value and onValueChange.

root-controlled-active-value.reason: Both report the next active item to the root callback after an arrow key: cmdk by value through value and onValueChange, modern-cmdk by item id through activeId and onActiveChange (modern-cmdk keys the active item by id, cmdk by value). cmdk then shows the new item active even though the parent kept value unchanged; modern-cmdk holds the controlled item.

dialog-open-structure.reason: Both render an open Dialog's overlay and content with the palette root, input, list and items inside the content.

dialog-aria.reason: Both dialogs are role="dialog" with the aria-label. modern-cmdk also labels the dialog with a visually hidden title, describes it with a visually hidden description, and gives the palette root role="search" with the label; cmdk's root inside the dialog has no role or label.

dialog-closed.reason: A Dialog with open false renders nothing in both.

dialog-overlay-dismiss.reason: A click on the overlay calls onOpenChange(false) once in both.

dialog-escape-reports.reason: One Escape calls onOpenChange(false) once in both.

server-items.reason: The server-rendered HTML lists every item in both.

server-empty-text.reason: cmdk's server HTML includes the Empty element and its text, so a server-rendered palette shows "no results" until it hydrates. modern-cmdk renders no Empty text on the server.
